conclusion: TokenJar snapshot alone is incomplete evidence for a collect-then-release strategy. Public collection can move existing pool protocol fees into the jar if the calling adapter is the current factory owner and its TOKEN_JAR matches the release jar. No collection grants the caller ownership before the UNI exchange.
next_question: A separately funded same-block pool discovery and active factory-owner check, then a fixed public collect eth_call with per-pool return accounting, can test the additional inventory. No source/runtime equivalence, harvest success, fee value, profitable release or inclusion is currently proved.

External collect accepts pool/amount requests without owner or feeSetter gating. It calls each pool collectProtocol with TOKEN_JAR as recipient and returns token0/token1 amounts. Administrative fee changes have separate authorization. FACTORY and TOKEN_JAR are immutable getters.
Same public collect path sends fees to TOKEN_JAR. Governance operations are separate; no fee-setting change is needed for already accumulated fees.

collect((address,uint128,uint128)[]) returns (uint128,uint128)[]. Each request specifies one pool and two requested native amounts. A successful batch supplies ordered per-pool amounts, not their cash value.
